s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging facial swelling with bony destruction
salient_findings: Diffuse, firm, non-tender mass on the left cheek
Vestibular swelling in the left oral cavity
Bony destruction of the maxillary alveolus on CT
key_facts: 52-year-old South Asian man
3-month history of swelling
Mass measures 4 × 5 cm
Mass extends from infraorbital region to lip commissure
Mass obliterates the nasal ala medially
Mass approaches the preauricular area laterally
Intraoral swelling measures 4 × 3 cm
Swelling extends from left canine to second molar
Normal hematologic parameters
CT shows mildly homogeneously enhancing soft-tissue density lesion
Incisional biopsy suggests myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common malignancy of the head and neck region, consistent with clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common salivary gland malignancy, possible given the location and swelling

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Incisional biopsy suggests lymphoid hyperplasia, making lymphoma a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive soft tissue sarcoma, possible given the rapid growth and bony destruction

shortlist.label: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common salivary gland malignancy, possible given the location and swelling, although less likely than squamous cell carcinoma

raw.rationale: The incisional biopsy suggests myositis with lymphoid hyperplasia, which is more consistent with lymphoma than the other options on the shortlist.

rejected.why: Biopsy results do not support this diagnosis
